raw.comments:
Issued as a Series D banknote by the Bank of Japan (Nippon Ginko) on July 19, 2000. Some western catalogs categorize it as a commemorative note for the 'End of the 2nd Millennium and the 26th G8 Summit in Okinawa' but it is considered a normal circulation note according to Japanese laws.
Because only few vending machines accept this note, and even numbers like 2 and 4 are seen as 'unlucky', this note circulates very rarely in comparison with the other denominations. An exception is Okinawa, where 40% of the 100 million (as of 2013) banknotes were issued.

The intaglio printed tactile marks at the bottom left and right of the front are the hiragana character に "ni" for two in Braille.

There are approximately 9000 J-L error notes that were released into general circulation. On the front of the note the prefix letter J appears in front of the serial number in the top left of the note, and the prefix letter L appears in front of the serial number at the bottom right of the note.

raw.comments:
Because of continuing inflation and the resulting increasing volume of A series 100 yen notes being issued, higher denomination bills became necessary. In addition, counterfeiting of poorly made A notes was rampant, and the B series 1,000 yen note was issued in 1950, ahead of other B notes.
It was the first Japanese banknote to use one or two letter prefix plus six numerals plus one letter postfix for the denomination, i.e., the same format used today, such as "A123456B" or "AB123456C" with a maximum serial number pool of 518,400,000 and 12,441,600,000 respectively.

Start of issue: 7th January 1950
End of issue: 4th January 1965

Banknotes with a serial number of 900001 or greater are replacement notes.

reverse.description:
Multicolour print (1 main colours and 6 background colours); red seal.
Exterior perspective of Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building on the left. Bank logo on top. Large denomination on top-right corner, and small one on bottom-left corner. Seal of the Director-General of the Bank of Japan's Currency Issue Department on bottom-center. Another exterior perspective of Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building on the bottom right.
EURion constellations on upper-left, and upper-right of the center window, one on the lower-right of large denomination, and another one on the right of the seal. Latent image 'NIPPON' appearing when look from bottom, below the large denomination. 'NIPPONGINKO' in microtext in the left of the frame.
